target.title: fix(auth): failed GitHub Copilot login keeps responses streaming
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users signing in to GitHub Copilot could leave a failed device-code or access-token HTTP response streaming after GitHub returned a non-success status. The login already surfaced the correct HTTP error, but the unread response connection stayed open.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared device-flow form helper now initiates cancellation of unread non-success bodies before releasing guarded-fetch resources, without waiting on the tee-sensitive cancellation promise used by debug capture. Cancellation remains best-effort so cleanup cannot delay or replace the existing labeled HTTP error; successful response parsing, request timeouts, domain routing, configuration, and public APIs are unchanged.

## User Impact

Failed GitHub Copilot login attempts now close their response streams promptly instead of retaining a live transport after the error is reported. Users continue to receive the same device-code or token HTTP error messages.

## Evidence

- Fresh regression red: the new cleanup-order assertion observed only `release` before the fix instead of the required `cancel`, then `release` sequence.
- Review-tail regression red: when a cloned debug-capture branch stayed open, release remained `pending` while the implementation awaited cancellation.
- Full focused test file: `extensions/github-copilot/login.test.ts` passes all 14 tests, including cleanup ordering, cancellation failure preserving `GitHub device code failed: HTTP 401`, and immediate release with an open cloned capture branch.
- Real streaming HTTP proof: the production `runGitHubCopilotDeviceFlow` entry point received a loopback streaming 401 response, preserved the labeled HTTP error, called guard release, did not show a device code, and closed the response before forced cleanup after only two server writes.
- Focused lint and formatting checks pass for the source and regression test.
- The extension-wide typecheck was not run locally: managed validation stopped before command execution because this host could not attest the required cgroup resource limits. No unbounded fallback was used; the remote CI lane remains responsible for that check.
